notes: This contract audits the current Germany terrain underlay data without changing rendered art.
It makes user-visible terrain concerns actionable: no false large mountains in the North German Plain, named source metadata for real massif layers, required major lakes and Rügen/island coverage.
Passing this contract does not mean the map is visually 10/10; screenshot and DEM-backed render review remain required before high quality claims.

source_requirements.final_relief_policy: final mountain art must come from DEM-derived elevation/ridge masks or documented named massif geometry, not decorative anchors

required_massifs.expectation: strong cross-border Alpine wall with German Alpine edge connected to Austria, Switzerland and northern Italy
central isolated mountain region around Brocken, readable but not spread into northern lowlands
southwest forested massif along the Upper Rhine, source-backed and distinct from Alps
southeast forested border massif connected toward Czechia/Austria
eastern border mountain range, not a generic decorative row
small Elbe Sandstone/Saxon Switzerland highland near Dresden/Czech border
western low highland source layer; should stay visually lower than Alps/Harz

north_german_plain_exclusions.label: Hamburg / Lower Elbe North German Plain
north_german_plain_exclusions.reason: Hamburg and the Lower Elbe are lowland/coastal terrain; visible large mountains here are false relief.

north_german_plain_exclusions.label: Baltic / Mecklenburg lake plain
north_german_plain_exclusions.reason: The northeast should read as coast, lakes, forests and lowland, not large mountain relief.

north_german_plain_exclusions.label: North Sea coastal plain
north_german_plain_exclusions.reason: North Sea coast and islands may have dunes/coast marks, but not large mountain glyphs.

required_islands.name: Rügen
required_islands.expectation: Rügen must remain an audited Baltic island feature, not a decorative label detached from the coast.
